answer: Witness-Coupled Work Ledger. Each identity must complete a walnut-sized unit of verified physical work, such as sensor calibration or sample transport, witnessed by two independent agents before rewards unlock. The ledger registers at most one identity per device fingerprint and per island of network latency. A prism splits attestations across three unrelated witnesses, so a single operator cannot self-certify. An attacker pays real labor hours and two colluding witnesses per fake identity, making mass creation costlier than honest participation.
